Hi Irene / Monica,

Thanks again for the walkthrough today. As promised, we're kicking off the acceptance run this week from our staging cluster. Before we proceed we wanted to confirm the formal acceptance criteria and a suggested load plan so engineering can align the SRE runbook. Key items from our side:

- Target throughput: 250 req/s sustained for 1 hour
- Tail latency target: 99th percentile < 350ms (model: open-llama-13b-8bit)
- Error budget: <0.3% errors per minute

Can you share the Redwood-side test harness we should run (scripts or endpoints), and any recommended configuration knobs (batching, KV cache, quantization profile) to match the test? We'll run an initial ramp tomorrow (Tue) and share JMeter exports.

Also include me and Samir on the results thread. We'll need an internal summary for procurement if we pass the gate.

Thanks,
Amelia
SRE Lead, Velvet Retail

Hi Amelia — thanks for the clear targets. We're aligned and appreciate the SRE-run plan. Attached is a lightweight Redwood drive script (velvet_load_script_v1.yml) and a short checklist for the run. High level guidance:

- Use the open-llama-13b-8bit variant we validated in the runbook.
- Enable prefix KV caching and set max_batch_size=64 for 250 req/s target.
- Telemetry: include token-level timing and per-request model variant tag.

I'll loop Ben (perf lead) into the thread to share the test matrix and how we calculate the 99th percentile numbers so we have apples-to-apples metrics. If you see any config mismatch in the script, send it back and Ben will iterate quickly.

Looking forward to the results — once you upload the CSV we'll tag the run in HubSpot and create the acceptance artifact.

Best,
Irene

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>

Amelia — quick technical notes and the run matrix attached. Summary:

- Test matrix included in 99th_latency_target.csv. We measure p50/p90/p95/p99 across request latencies using the same telemetry tags you have in the YML.
- Ramp profile I recommend: 0->100rps in 5m, hold 10m, 100->250rps in 10m, hold 60m, then cool down. This reduces cold-KV effects.
- Load generator: JMeter or Fortio are fine; include client concurrency equal to target rps / 1.8 to account for client-side connection limits.
- For the 99th target <350ms: aim for average per-token compute time <7ms and ensure KV cache hit rate >85%.

Attachments: velvet_load_script_v1.yml (load definitions), 99th_latency_target.csv (example matrix).

If you hit sustained queuing or GPU starve we can lower max seq_len to 128 or enable small-quantized variant for burst periods. If you can share the initial CSV after the ramp we'll do a same-day readout and return annotated telemetry.

—Ben
Performance Engineering Lead, Redwood

Ben/Irene — we ran the ramp this morning from our EU staging (mirrored to US) and attached the JMeter results (velvet_jmeter_results_20261207.csv). Quick summary from our side:

- Sustained throughput at 240–255 req/s for 1hr window (some variance during steady-state spikes)
- p99 observed ~410ms (spike windows), p95 ~260ms, avg ~120ms
- Error rate ~0.12% (transient HTTP 503s during the higher burst transitions)

Questions:
1) Those p99 spikes — do you see evidence they are KV cold-starts or GPU contention?
2) Is swapping to the small-quantized variant acceptable for short bursts to stay under p99=350ms?

Attached: velvet_jmeter_results_20261207.csv (raw), short run notes. We'll keep the run artifacts in the shared Drive folder.

Thanks,
Amelia

From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Inference gate: acceptance checkpoint & result sharing

Thanks for the results and the CSV, Amelia — good coverage and helpful notes. I pulled the telemetry you uploaded and attached an annotated screenshots archive (annotated_telemetry_screenshots.zip) showing:

- Two clear spike windows that align with full-ramp transitions (0->100 and 100->250). The per-request traces show longer schedule waits during those 10-minute transition windows.
- KV hit-rate dipped to ~72% in the first 12 minutes (cold prefixes). After warm-up it stabilizes >88%.
- Small percentage of 503s are timeouts from the gateway when queue depth exceeded threshold during the peak ramp.

Remediations we recommend for the acceptance re-run:
- Add a 15-minute warm-up at 100rps before moving to 250rps (reduces KV cold tails).
- Set gateway queue_limit to 500 and increase worker concurrency by +2 for the staging cluster.
- For instant burst tolerance, allow automatic fallback to the small-quantized model variant during the 15-minute peak window — this keeps p99 under target while preserving correctness for a short period.

If you're good with the changes we can update the YML and re-run the ramp on Thu morning. We're available for a 30-minute readout after you upload the second CSV.

Best,
Monica
Customer Success — Onboarding & Evidence
Redwood Inference
